zh.question: 细菌这么小，它也有细胞膜和 DNA 吗？
zh.observe: 固定选择细胞膜或 DNA，依次切换动物、叶肉植物和细菌；再比较细胞核、叶绿体的有无。观察“没有细胞核”与“没有遗传信息”的区别。

academic.title: 共同特征比外形更能定义细胞
academic.body: 细胞是生物体结构与功能的基本单位，细胞膜把内部与外部区分，并参与物质交换和内部环境维持。细胞质中的分子体系进行代谢，核糖体参与蛋白质合成，DNA 保存遗传信息。具体细胞可以高度特化而失去某些结构，例如成熟哺乳动物红细胞，所以“典型细胞图”是比较框架，不是每一个现实细胞都具备全部标配的承诺。

academic.title: 有无核膜区分不同组织方式
academic.body: 动物和植物的典型细胞具有膜包围的细胞核，大部分 DNA 在其中；线粒体及植物叶绿体还含有少量自身 DNA。细菌没有这样的细胞核，主要 DNA 集中在拟核区域，但仍是具有膜、细胞质和核糖体的细胞。拟核不是一个缩小版的细胞核，判断关键是有没有核膜，而不是把 DNA 画成圆圈还是弯曲线条。

academic.title: 植物细胞要说明取样部位
academic.body: 叶肉细胞中的叶绿体进行光合作用，较大的液泡和细胞壁也影响空间与形状，但许多根细胞没有叶绿体。植物细胞同样拥有线粒体并进行呼吸；细胞壁在细胞膜外，不能把二者当作同一个边界。比较图为了可读性把三种细胞画到相近大小，因此只能比较结构，不能据图推断细菌和叶肉细胞的真实尺寸相同。

zh.misconception: 细菌没有细胞核，但有 DNA，而且细菌本身就是细胞；并非每个植物细胞都有叶绿体。
zh.boundary: 代表细胞经过配色、放大和结构取舍；不按同一尺度，也没有表现分子拥挤或所有细胞器，不能当作显微镜的直接视野。

narration.label: 把世界看得更小
narration.text: 我们的身体、树叶，还有许多小生物，都和细胞有关。细胞很小，通常需要工具才能仔细看。今天的图把它们放大，还加上颜色，方便我们认识。先看看动物细胞，再看看叶子里的细胞：形状不一样，却都有一条把里面和外面分开的边界。
narration.cue: 展示动物和叶肉细胞，选择细胞膜。

narration.label: 会交换的边界
narration.text: 这条边界叫细胞膜。它不只是把东西包起来，还参与调节一些物质的进出。植物细胞的膜外面，通常另有一层细胞壁，帮助支撑。现在换成细菌，停一停，找找它有没有膜。看，小小的细菌也有这样的边界，所以细菌自己就是一个细胞。

narration.label: 信息放在哪里
narration.text: 再找找 DNA，它保存着遗传信息。动物和植物的典型细胞里，大部分 DNA 住在有膜围着的细胞核中。细菌没有这种细胞核，可不是没有 DNA；它的信息放在细胞内的一个区域。就像有没有一个单独的房间，和有没有重要的东西，是两个不同的问题。
narration.cue: 保持 DNA 选中，对比三种细胞，再选细胞核。

narration.label: 绿色小结构的工作
narration.text: 叶肉细胞里还有绿色的叶绿体，帮助植物利用光来制造糖。但植物根部的许多细胞没有叶绿体，不能把整株植物里的每个细胞都画成绿色。今天我们看的大小也经过调整，方便比较。学会找共同点和不同点，比记住每张图上有几个彩色小圆圈更有意思。
narration.cue: 选择叶绿体，比较叶肉与动物、细菌。

en.question: Can a tiny bacterium have a cell membrane and DNA too?
en.observe: Keep membrane or DNA selected while switching among animal, leaf and bacterial cells. Then compare nuclei and chloroplasts, distinguishing the absence of a nucleus from the absence of genetic information.

academic.title: Shared organisation matters more than outline
academic.body: Cells are basic units of biological organisation. Membranes separate inside from outside and regulate exchange; molecular systems support metabolism, ribosomes make proteins and DNA carries hereditary information. Specialised cells can lose structures, as mature mammalian red blood cells do, so a typical diagram is a comparison framework rather than a universal checklist.

academic.title: A nuclear envelope distinguishes organisation
academic.body: Typical animal and plant cells have a membrane-bound nucleus containing most DNA, with additional DNA in mitochondria and chloroplasts. Bacteria lack a nucleus; much of their DNA occupies a nucleoid region. A nucleoid is not a miniature nucleus: the crucial distinction is the enclosing membrane, not the shape used to draw DNA.

academic.title: Plant-cell claims need a tissue context
academic.body: Leaf mesophyll cells contain photosynthetic chloroplasts, whereas many root cells do not. Plant cells also contain mitochondria and respire. A wall lies outside the membrane rather than replacing it. Cells are enlarged to similar screen sizes for structural comparison, not shown at a common scale.

en.misconception: Bacteria lack a nucleus but contain DNA and are cells. Not every plant cell contains chloroplasts.
en.boundary: Representative cells are coloured, enlarged and simplified. They are not equally scaled or literal microscope views, and omit molecular crowding and many organelles.

narration.label: Look at a smaller world
narration.text: Our bodies, leaves and many tiny organisms are made of cells. Cells usually need special tools to examine closely. Our pictures enlarge and colour them to help us learn. Compare an animal cell with a leaf cell: their shapes differ, but both have a boundary between inside and outside.
narration.cue: Compare animal and leaf cells with membrane selected.

narration.label: A boundary that allows exchange
narration.text: The cell membrane helps regulate what enters and leaves. Plant cells also have a supporting wall outside that membrane. Switch to a bacterium and pause to find its membrane. It has this kind of boundary too: a bacterium is itself a cell.
narration.cue: Switch to bacteria and pause at the membrane.

narration.label: Where is information kept?
narration.text: Find DNA, which stores hereditary information. In typical animal and plant cells, most DNA is inside a membrane-bound nucleus. Bacteria lack that kind of nucleus but still have DNA in a region inside the cell. Having a separate room and having important contents are different questions.
narration.cue: Compare DNA in all three cells, then select nucleus.

narration.label: The green structures
narration.text: Leaf cells contain chloroplasts that help use light to make sugars. Many root cells have none, so not every cell in a plant should be painted green. We adjusted drawing sizes to make comparison easier. Finding shared features and differences matters more than memorising coloured shapes.
narration.cue: Compare chloroplast presence across the examples.
